conventions.convention: Covariate shift requires supplied conditional label kernels agreeing as probability measures outside one measurable target-marginal-null set, together with absolute continuity of the target input marginal with respect to the source input marginal. Conditional kernels are not asserted to exist automatically.
Domain risks are extended nonnegative integrals of product-measurable losses composed with measurable predictors; finite risk is not implicit.
The H-delta-H divergence is twice the supremum of absolute disagreement-probability differences over a nonempty class of measurable binary classifiers, and lies in [0,2].
Every pairwise loss integral entering the discrepancy must be finite, but their supremum may be infinite and need not be attained.

The importance weight is the target-input density relative to the source-input law. The joint-density lemma and importance-weighting theorem explicitly assume AC; the latter concludes a finite identity under integrability of the weighted source loss.
The joint-labeling error is the infimum of the sum of source and target binary risks over H. No attained minimizer, covariate shift, or empirical-risk substitution is assumed.

In the discrepancy theorem P denotes the source input law and Q the target input law; the displayed bound controls L_P(h,f_P). The loss is symmetric and satisfies the triangle inequality, both stated minimizers exist, and labeling risks may be infinite.

load_bearing.statement: Source and target are joint probability laws on a common measurable input-label product. Covariate shift requires specified conditional label kernels agreeing outside a target-marginal-null measurable set and target-input absolute continuity with respect to the source-input law.

Assume AC. For source and target joint laws with specified conditional label kernels agreeing outside a target-input-null set and target-input absolute continuity, every nonnegative measurable representative w of the target-input/source-input Radon–Nikodym derivative satisfies P_T(E) = integral_E w(x) dP_S for every product-measurable E. Consequently P_T is absolutely continuous with respect to P_S, with joint density w composed with the input projection.

Assume AC. Under covariate shift with the stated common conditional label kernel, for any measurable predictor and nonnegative product-measurable loss, integrability of the source loss weighted by a nonnegative representative of dμ_T/dμ_S implies that target risk equals that weighted source integral and is finite.
For probability input laws and a nonempty measurable binary classifier class H, d_HΔH(μ_S,μ_T) = 2 sup_{h,h′ in H} |μ_S(A_{h,h′}) − μ_T(A_{h,h′})|.

For joint binary-label probability laws with input marginals μ_S,μ_T and nonempty measurable classifier class H, set λ = inf_{g in H}(ε_S(g)+ε_T(g)). Every h in H satisfies ε_T(h) ≤ ε_S(h) + ½d_HΔH(μ_S,μ_T) + λ.

For probability input laws P,Q, a nonempty measurable hypothesis class and a nonnegative product-measurable loss, assume all pairwise loss integrals under P and Q are finite. Define disc_L(P,Q) as the supremum over hypothesis pairs of their absolute integrated-loss difference, allowing an infinite supremum.

For source and target input laws P,Q, measurable labeling functions, a nonempty measurable hypothesis class, a nonnegative measurable symmetric triangle-inequality loss, finite pairwise hypothesis risks and attained source and target minimizers h_P*,h_Q*, every h in H satisfies L_P(h,f_P) ≤ L_P(h_P*,f_P) + L_Q(h,h_Q*) + disc_L(P,Q) + min{L_Q(h_Q*,h_P*),L_P(h_Q*,h_P*)}, interpreted in the extended nonnegative reals.

seams_checked.note: This is a contextual page prerequisite. No assigned proof invokes a Rademacher theorem. The population-bound remarks correctly require separate bounded-loss and complexity assumptions for empirical substitutions; they assert no unsupported finite-sample bound.

The page prerequisite is contextual. Its contrastive-loss definition and zero-shot classification algorithm invoke no adaptation inequality; the algorithm explicitly makes no accuracy or distribution-generalization guarantee.

The foundation-model definition repeats the exact supplied-kernel, target-null-set and target/source absolute-continuity conditions without asserting kernel existence. Its companion interface example correctly identifies disjoint support as violating covariate shift and claims no transfer guarantee.

The actual source-target citation in ex-calibration-degradation-under-shift uses only the joint-law definition. Its clean/corrupted construction keeps source and target laws distinct and explicitly identifies failure of calibration/test exchangeability; it does not invoke importance weighting or claim coverage under arbitrary shift.
